sentences.text: JUDGMENT
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

Brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 24-07-2022 at about 10-30 p.m. the petitioner was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-02/JE-2725 from Petrol Bunk towards Vidyaranyapura on the extreme left side on HMT Main road, Bengaluru city, when he reached in front of Kadamba Hotel, at that time, driver of Hyundai Car bearing registration No.KA-01/MX-1389 parked the said vehicle negligently without indicator, that too in the late hours, as a result of which the petitioner dashed the back side of said Car and sustained grievous injuries.
3. It is further stated that, immediately he was shifted to Omega Multispecialty Hospital, Yelahanka for first aid, then he was shifted to K.I.M.S. hospital, Bengaluru for further treatment, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards transportation, treatment,
medicines, conveyance etc.,
4.

It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and working as Sales Manager in Indian Petrol Bunk, Jalahalli, Bengaluru and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5.
It is stated that, the accident occurred due to negligent act of driver of the Hyundai Car bearing Registration No.KA-01/MX-1389.
Hence the Jalahalli Traffic Police have filed charge sheet against driver of said vehicle in Cr.No.72/2022.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After service of summons, respondent No.1 and 2 appeared through their respective counsel and filed the written statements.

7. In the written statement the respondent No.1 stated that he is the RC Owner of the the Hyundai Car bearing Registration No.KA-01/MX-1389 and the said vehicle was insured with respondent No.2 and policy was in force as on the date of accident and the driver of offending vehicle had valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition Mohan Kumar B.S vs Divakar M. Narayana on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69123199/
2 with cost.
8.

sentences.text: In the written statement, the respondent No.2 admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Hyundai Car bearing registration No.KA-01/MX-1389 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contended that, the driver of offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

It is contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner, as he was not wearing the safety head gear Further stated that there is delay in lodging the complaint.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

9. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 24.7.2022 at about 10.30 p.m. on HMT Main Road, in front of Kadamba Hotel, Bengaluru due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Hyundai Car bearing registration No.KA-01- MX-1389 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate? from whom?
3. What order or award?
ADDITIONAL ISSUE:-
1. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the respondent No.1 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy?
10.
In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P13.

In addition to his evidence, placed the evidence of Dr.Jayaram B.S. as PW2 and got marked documents at Ex.P14 to Ex.P16.
11.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1.
12.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.

My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Addl.Issue No.1 : In the Negative Issue No.2: Partly in Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S ISSUE No.1:
14.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Hyundai Car bearing registration No.KA- 01/MX-1389 the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

15. On the other hand, the respondents have contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner only and not on the part of the driver of the Hyundai Car bearing registration No.KA-01/MX-1389.
16.
In the light of the rival contentions of both the parties, on going through the above issue burden is on the petitioner to prove the above issue on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
17. The petitioner in order to prove his case got examined himself as PW1.
He has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the police documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P3, Ex.P6 to Ex.P9.

Ex.P1-true copy of FIR, Ex.P2- true copy of FIS, Ex.P3- true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P6-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P7-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P8-true copy of spot sketch & Ex.P9-true copy of charge sheet.

18. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that based upon the first information statement given by the petitioner, registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 283 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the Investigation Officer of the case has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 283 and 338 of IPC.
19.
In order to substantiate the defence of the respondent No.2 has examined its Legal Manager as RW1.

He has deposed in his evidence that, there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-01-MX-1389, the car was parked on the extreme left side of the road by taking all precautions, at that time, the petitioner being the rider of the motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner by carrying Silver Can infront of the motor cycle and dashed against the rear portion of the car.
The petitioner lodged false complaint after lapse of two days and the jurisdictional police have filed false charge sheet without proper investigation.
In the cross- examination he has admitted that they have not challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the car.
20. On perusal of evidence of RW1, it is crystal clear that they have not challenged the charge sheet filed against the driver of the car.
Moreover they have not made an effort to examine driver of the offending vehicle i.e., the respondent No.1.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 except filing Mohan Kumar B.S vs Divakar M. Narayana on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69123199/
4 written statement has not stepped into the witness box to prove his defence.

sentences.text: The respondents except making allegations they have not placed any relevant documents to disprove the allegations made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

21. Apart from this, even at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defences of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.

22. In the light of the evidence placed on record, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-01-MX-1389.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ADDITIONAL ISSUE :
23.
This issue is with respect to the violation of fundamental conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.2 has stated that the driver of the car bearing No.KA-01-MX-1389 had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Hence, respondent No.1 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy.
In this regard, except the allegation in the written statement the respondent No.2 has not placed sufficient documents to prove its contention.
Hence, it is clear that the respondent No.2 has failed to prove that the respondent No.1 has violated the fundamental conditions of the policy.
Hence, I answer the Additional issue is in the Negative.

ISSUE No.2:
24.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

25. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining Mohan Kumar B.S vs Divakar M. Narayana on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69123199/
5 quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.

sentences.text: That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P3.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Tenderness and swelling present over left knee joint region X-ray shows proximal tibia fracture 27.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that, the said injury is grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary issued by KIMS Hospital as per Ex.P4, which reveals that petitioner was admitted to the said Hospital from 25.7.2022 to 27.7.2022.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.B.S.Jayaram as PW2.
He has deposed that the petitioner has sustained proximal tibia fracture.
He has placed inpatient record, outpatient record and x- rays as per Ex.P14 to Ex.P16.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he might have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
28.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a Sales Manager at Indian Petrol Bunk, Bengaluru and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard, there is no iota of documents to show the income of the petitioner.
Hence, in the absence of the documents, it is apt to take the notional income as per law.
On perusal of discharge summary issued by KIMS Hospital as per Ex.P4, which reveals that petitioner was admitted to the said Hospital from 25.7.2022 to 27.7.2022.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of one month by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.

Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,500/-
towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
29.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P12 to the extent of Rs.46,992/-.
Except the suguestion there are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.46,992/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
30.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.
Loss of future income;
31. The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.B.S.Jayaram, examined as PW2.
He has stated in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained proximal tibia fracture, for which he underwent ORIF with plate and screws to left tibia by MIPPO technique.

In support of his evidence he has produced inpatient record, outpatient record and x-rays at Ex.P14 to Ex.P16.
32.

Further, PW2 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner, petitioner has pain over left knee joint, swelling of the left knee joint, limp on the left side, difficult to stand for long time, swelling of the left knee joint and surgical scar mark present over the medial aspect of the left knee.
PW2 has assessed permanent physical disability at 27.38%.
33. In the cross-examination he has admitted that fracture is united.
Further denied the suggestion that he has assessed the disability on higher side in order to help the petitioner.
34. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW2 as physical disability is at 27.38%.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 10%
instead of 27.38%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
35. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 32 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card and driving licence at Ex.P10 & Ex.P11 for consideration.
On perusal of the said documents, his date of birth is mentioned as 4.6.1989.
The alleged accident occurred on 24.7.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 33 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '16' is to be taken into consideration.

36. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was working as a Sales Manager at Indian Petrol Bunk,
Bengaluru and getting an income of Rs.25,000/- per month.

sentences.text: iota of documents.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.

37. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X 12 X 16 X10/100= Rs.2,97,600/-.
Loss of amenities;
38.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to walk, stand long time, limping while walking, not able to sit cross leg and not able to use Indian toilet.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
39.
PW2 has stated that petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost around Rs.30,000/-.
Either PW1 or PW2 have not placed any estimation in this regard.

On going through the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also escalation of rates in the medical field, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medication.

LIABILITY:
42.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing registration No.KA-01-MX-1389 the alleged accident had taken place.

The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1,
remained unshaken.

As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
43. As per the records, the insurance policy is valid.
As such, I am of the view that, the respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
44.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.4,35,092/- (Rupees four lakhs thirty thousand and ninety two only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
